why:
TWO ROWS CLOSED, and they are batched into one PR deliberately: this lane measured today that `main` moves on docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json roughly every 4 minutes while `pytest-run` takes ~20 (n=2: 20m47s on #11979, 19m26s on #12061), so a register-touching PR is in a race it can lose. Two closures of the same concern -- draining rows -- in one PR halves the exposure. Tier-1 throughout: docs/**, tests/**, .github/**. No src/, no config, no order path.

(1) BL-20260902-A-REBASE-ARMS-AUTOMERGE-BECAUSE-A-PUSH-DIFF-INCLUDES-EVERYTHING-MAIN-CHANGED -- RESOLVED, AND IT WAS FIXED TEN DAYS AGO AND NEVER CLOSED. Commit 2816698ac (2026-09-02 18:49Z, 'automerge: gate the relay on the branch's OWN request, and stop it un-drafting') did the work; the row has read as an open live-PR hazard since. VERIFIED AGAINST origin/main, not my working tree: the legacy `.github/pr-automerge-request` is absent (`git cat-file -e` fails) and the string occurs **0** times in the workflow, whose paths filter is `.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt` alone -- criterion (a), both halves. Criterion (b) is ALSO implemented though not required: the job body resolves `<slug>.txt`, reads its blob sha at the pushed head AND at main, and returns doing nothing when it is absent ('this push matched the paths filter through another branch's request file') or byte-identical ('this branch inherited it rather than asking'), using two getContent calls because 'the event's list is the thing that is wrong', and RE-RAISING a non-404 read error because 'a read we could not make is NOT proof of absence'. The independent clause is satisfied and it REFUSES rather than logs: `if (!created && pr.draft) { ...; return; }`. ⚠️ THE CRITERION'S WARNING IS MOOT ON MAIN AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMING: it forbids closing by deleting tests/test_zz_automerge_hold.py. That file is absent, but `git log origin/main -- tests/test_zz_automerge_hold.py` returns **0 commits** -- it lived and died on a branch and never reached main, so its absence is not that route. I did NOT measure whether #10789 was re-armed on its own branch in the gap between the hold's removal (12:26Z) and the fix (18:49Z); that is a question about that PR, and asserting it settled would be the unverified claim this row is about. ⚠️ AND THIS SESSION EXERCISED THE FIX WITHOUT SETTING OUT TO: three of my branches read as UNARMED once their own request files reached main, because pr-landing-guard R6 applies the same byte-identical-to-main test.

(2) BL-20260909-SESSION-BOARD-SCHEMA-DOCUMENTS-A-PR-FIELD-THAT-THE-CLAIM-TOOL-REFUSES-AND-CI-REDS-ON -- RESOLVED via criterion (a), and THE DRIFT WAS TWO-WAY, which the row did not see. Re-verified by RUNNING the writer: schema.merge_slot declared `pr: <int|null>` and claim_merge_slot.py contains `"pr"` **0** times -- the row's half. The same read showed `build_claim` returns exactly {held_by, branch, claimed_at, purpose}, writing `purpose` on EVERY claim, while the schema declared no `purpose` at all -- and the live merge_slot on the board carries it right now. So the documented shape named a key never written AND omitted one always written. The schema string is corrected as a single-line replace, not a re-serialisation, because a whole-file rewrite of that hot register is the exact hazard its size test guards.

THE SEPARATE HALF THE ROW FLAGGED IS DONE TOO, because it is the same lesson one level up: test_real_board_diff_is_small_enough_to_conflict_narrowly asserted the CAUSE 'A whole-file re-serialisation turns every concurrent session edit into a conflict' -- which its POSITIONAL line-zip cannot distinguish from a single inserted line, since an insertion shifts everything after it and scores identically. That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A; CLAUDE.md's remedy is to report the quantity rather than reword the label, so the message now carries the line counts and warns that the metric is positional.

STRUCTURAL HALF, so it cannot drift a third time: test_schema_string_matches_what_build_claim_actually_writes parses the schema string's key names and asserts they equal set(build_claim(...)). MUTATION-TESTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- re-introducing `pr` fails it, deleting `purpose` fails it; the clean tree passes 19/19. Its message says the WRITER is authoritative (field beats comment) so the next session fixes the right surface. ⚠️ That also meets the row's own objection that 'a green run does NOT clear this row: the suite is green whenever nobody has added the documented key' -- the new test fails on the DOCUMENT rather than on a caller happening to exercise it, so green now means the two surfaces agree.

⚠️ WHY THE STRUCTURAL HALF MATTERS MORE THAN THE ONE-LINE FIX: a doc wrong in the PERMISSIVE direction costs more than a missing one. A session that FOLLOWED the documented shape added `pr` and was told by a red test it had reformatted the whole file, losing a full ~16-minute CI cycle chasing a reformat that never happened.
